tool.name: HyphAeon-Temporal
tool.description: Continuous temporal selection regression, two-stage filtering, and dynamic wave decomposition
tool.command: @SYMLINK_FILES@ #if $dates_file: ln -s '$dates_file' dates_input.tsv && #end if hyphaeon temporal -a input.$input_file.extension @INPUT_TREE@ @MODEL_VARIANT@ #if $max_species: -s $max_species #end if #if $dates_file: -d dates_input.tsv #if $date_col: --date-col '$date_col' #end if #if $strain_col: --strain-col '$strain_col' #end if #end if #if $root_taxon: --root-taxon '$root_taxon' #end if #if $bandwidth: -bw $bandwidth #end if -B $n_permutations --perm-alpha $perm_alpha --min-r2 $min_r2 --tau-peak $tau_peak #if $tau_auc: --tau-auc $tau_auc #end if --time-points $time_points --time-units $time_units --sweep-mode $sweep_mode $keep_duplicates $plot -o 'temporal_output'

param.label: Maximum species (optional)
param.help: Maximum number of taxa to include (farthest-point traversal subsampling if exceeded)

param.name: dates_file
param.label: Sampling dates file (optional)
param.help: Nextstrain Auspice JSON, or metadata CSV/TSV mapping taxa to collection dates. If omitted, HyphAeon attempts to auto-extract timestamps from FASTA headers.

param.name: date_col
param.label: Date column name
param.help: Name of the collection date column in the metadata CSV/TSV (required if using a CSV/TSV dates file without a standard column name)

param.name: strain_col
param.label: Strain column name
param.help: Name of the taxon/strain identifier column in the metadata CSV/TSV

param.name: root_taxon
param.label: Root/founder taxon (optional)
param.help: Reference taxon to use as ancestral root founder (default: consensus of earliest 5%% sampled taxa)

param.label: Gaussian kernel bandwidth (years)
param.help: Smoothing bandwidth in years for the temporal regression kernel. Default: auto ~5%% of timespan.

param.label: Number of permutations
param.help: Number of date-shuffling permutations for Stage 2 empirical p-values

param.label: Permutation FDR cutoff
param.help: FDR significance cutoff for the Stage 2 permutation test

param.label: Min wave alignment R²
param.help: Minimum dynamic wave alignment R² threshold for confirmed sweeps

param.label: Stage 1 peak energy floor
param.help: Stage 1 peak selection intensity energy floor

param.label: Temporal grid points
param.help: Number of continuous temporal grid points for the regression

param.label: Generate publication figures
param.help: Generate 4-panel PDF and PNG figures showing temporal selection dynamics

param.label: Stage 1 AUC energy floor (optional)
param.help: Stage 1 cumulative area under curve energy floor (default: auto)

param.label: Time units
param.help: Time coordinate of sample timestamps. Non-'years' disables calendar-year gate and kernel ceiling — required for experimental-evolution / LTEE generation axes

param.label: Sweep mode
param.help: 'episodic': positive velocity max(0,da/dt) (viral turnover). 'fixation': cumulative amplitude shift (experimental-evolution permanent fixation). 'auto': fixation when time-units != years, else episodic

param.label: Keep duplicate sequences
param.help: Do not collapse identical longitudinal clones before regression (auto-enabled when time-units != years)

tool.help:
HyphAeon Temporal: Continuous Temporal Selection Surveillance ===============================================================
**What question does this method answer?**
How has selection pressure on individual codon sites changed over time within a serially-sampled viral or pathogen population? Which sites show significant temporal selection trends, and can these be decomposed into dynamic selection waves?
**How it works**
HyphAeon Temporal performs continuous temporal attribution regression on serially-sampled sequence data:
1. **Temporal Regression**: Uses collection dates (from metadata or auto-extracted from FASTA headers) to construct a continuous temporal grid. For each codon site, regresses the model's selection signal against sampling time using a Gaussian kernel smoother.
2. **Two-Stage Statistical Filtering**:
- *Stage 1*: Energy floor filtering using peak selection intensity (τ_peak) and cumulative area under the curve (τ_auc). - *Stage 2*: Date-shuffling permutation test for empirical p-values, controlling for phylogenetic confounding of temporal signal.
3. **Dynamic Wave Decomposition**: Decomposes temporal selection curves into component waves using functional PCA. Sites with sufficient wave alignment (R² ≥ min_r2) are flagged as confirmed sweeps.
**Inputs**
- An in-frame codon alignment (FASTA or NEXUS) with serially-sampled taxa - An optional phylogenetic tree - Optional sampling dates (Nextstrain Auspice JSON or metadata CSV/TSV). If omitted, dates are auto-extracted from FASTA headers.
**Outputs**
- **Sites summary (CSV)**: per-site temporal selection statistics - **Curves (CSV)**: continuous temporal selection curves across the grid - **Waves (CSV)**: dynamic wave decomposition components - **Summary (JSON)**: overall surveillance summary including significant sites and confirmed sweeps - **Plot (PDF/PNG)**: optional 4-panel publication figure
